Create a PeakAnnotationISF object

Source: R/constructor_createPeakAnnotationISF.R
createPeakAnnotationISF.Rd

User-facing constructor for PeakAnnotationISF-class.

Tier naming:

  • Tier 1c — MS2 fragment match, intra-group (Phase 1)

  • Tier 1c_ext — MS2 fragment match, RT-gated features (Phase 2)

Priority: 1a > 1b > 1c > 1d > 2. MS2 tier (1c) only assigned when no higher-priority tier already fired.

Parent features are identified by parent_col/parent_val:

  • parent_val = NULL (default): any non-empty, non-NA string in parent_col is a parent (e.g. PI_match column containing compound name strings).

  • Otherwise: exact match parent_col == parent_val.

Usage

createPeakAnnotationISF(
  phase1_result,
  ms2_list,
  FT,
  parent_col = "PI_match",
  parent_val = NULL,
  ppm_isf = 10,
  mz_threshold_isf = 0.005,
  rt_isf_threshold = 5
)

Arguments

phase1_result

data.frame. Output of annotateLibMatch(). Required columns: feature_name, Lib_group, mz, and parent_col. Optional: rt.

ms2_list

list. From read_ms2_consensus().

FT

data.frame. Full MS1 feature tabel. Required: feature_name, mzmed/mz. Optional: rtmed/rt.

parent_col

Character. Column identifying parent features. Default "PI_match".

parent_val

Value marking a parent. NULL = any non-empty string. Default NULL.

ppm_isf

Numeric. ppm tolerance. Default 10.

mz_threshold_isf

Numeric. Absolute m/z floor (Da). Default 0.005.

rt_isf_threshold

Numeric. RT window (seconds). Default 5.

Value

A PeakAnnotationISF-class object.

See also

annotateISF(), PeakAnnotationISF-class, read_ms2_consensus()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ms2_list <- read_ms2_consensus(ms2_consensus, feature_table = FT)

isf_obj <- createPeakAnnotationISF(
  phase1_result    = pool_annotate_res_ms1,
  ms2_list         = ms2_list,
  FT          = FT,
  parent_col       = "PI_match",
  ppm_isf          = 10,
  rt_isf_threshold = 5.0
)
isf_result <- annotateISF(isf_obj)
} # }
